title: specwright — v1: platform-agnostic spec-driven development plugin
description:
# specwright — v1: platform-agnostic spec-driven development plugin

## Problem Statement

The user has built a personal spec-driven development workflow stitched from several skills (`/grill-me`, `/tdd`, `/to-prd`, `/prd-to-issues`, ralph loops invoked via shell scripts). It works in isolation but has six concrete gaps:

1. **No parallelism.** Multiple PRDs in flight can't fan out; ralph loops run one slice at a time.
2. **No flow differentiation.** Feature work, bugfixes, and tiny tickets all go through the same heavyweight grilling — wasteful for small work, insufficient for bugs (no diagnose step, no regression-test guarantee).
3. **TDD drifts to implementation tests.** The existing `/tdd` skill doesn't enforce intent-based tests; tests end up coupled to internal calls instead of user-visible behavior.
4. **Auto-verify is manual.** Tests, lint, format, and typecheck aren't automatically run at task end; the agent leaves verification to the user.
5. **Code review is ad-hoc.** No structured multi-reviewer fan-out, no severity grading, no auto-fix offer for critical findings.
6. **Not portable.** The workflow depends on the user's personal `~/.claude/skills/` collection. Colleagues, fresh machines, and Codex users get nothing.

A hackday with serversia proved one-shot SDD works but produced bloated, unreviewable code. Kiro's three-phase artifact model (requirements / design / tasks) is the right shape but Kiro is closed and not portable across agents.

## Solution

**specwright** — a platform-agnostic plugin of markdown skills delivering Kiro-style three-phase SDD with the six gaps above closed:

- **Four explicit entry flows** for different sizes of work: `feature` (full PRD), `bugfix` (diagnose-first + mandatory regression-test slice), `quick` (one-pass auto-gen with surfaced assumptions), `tiny` (no PRD, brief grill, beads-only).
- **Hybrid spec storage:** PRDs on disk in `.specs/<slug>/` (PR-reviewable as code); tasks in beads (dependency graph drives parallelism).
- **Vertical-slice parallelism** via git worktrees: one AC per slice; `depends_on` edges in beads; fan-out launches non-overlapping cohorts; chains become stacked PRs.
- **Six-step per-slice execute pipeline** with intent-based TDD and a bounded auto-verify loop (N=3 retries).
- **Four-subagent severity-graded review** with a tabular report and a numbered auto-fix prompt for CRITICAL/HIGH findings.
- **Single auto-attempt PR-rebase conflict resolution** when a sibling PR merges and changes a chained PR's base.
- **Distributed as one repo with two marketplace manifests:** Claude Code plugin marketplace listing + self-hosted Codex `marketplace.json` at the repo root. Same `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` files underneath; portable via `git clone` for any other agent.

## User Stories

1. As a developer starting a sizable feature, I want to run a guided three-phase flow (grill → PRD → slice → execute) so that the implementation matches genuine design intent.
2. As a developer fixing a known bug, I want a diagnose-first flow that writes a `bugfix.md` with Current / Expected / Unchanged Behavior so that the fix is surgical and regression-proof.
3. As a developer fixing a bug, I want a mandatory regression-test slice that fails before the fix so that the bug can never silently re-emerge.
4. As a developer with a clear small ask, I want a `tiny` flow that skips the PRD entirely so that I don't bureaucratize a typo fix.
5. As a developer with an obviously-shaped feature, I want a `quick` flow that auto-generates all PRD artifacts in one pass so that I save the grilling time when I already know what I want.
6. As a developer using quick flow, I want every assumption the agent made surfaced in a dated `## Assumptions` section so that I can correct course before execution.
7. As a developer launching parallel work, I want ready slices to fan out into independent worktrees automatically so that I can pipeline multiple slices end-to-end concurrently.
8. As a developer with dependent slices, I want chained PRs stacked (each PR's base = parent slice's branch) so that reviewers can see the chain.
9. As a developer running parallel slices, I want path-overlap detection to serialize would-conflict slices into non-overlapping cohorts so that I don't manufacture merge conflicts.
10. As a developer whose sibling PR just merged, I want the next PR in the chain to auto-rebase and auto-resolve simple conflicts so that the AFK flow keeps moving.
11. As a developer writing tests, I want the TDD skill to enforce intent-based tests against user-visible behavior so that my tests don't ossify implementation details.
12. As a developer finishing a slice, I want the auto-verify loop (test / lint / format / typecheck / build) to run automatically before the PR opens so that the PR is clean by construction.
13. As a developer when verify fails, I want the agent to retry up to N=3 times then mark the slice `blocked` in beads with the failure attached so that I don't lose context on hard failures.
14. As a developer opening a PR, I want a four-subagent fan-out review (spec-alignment, test-quality, code-quality+security, vertical-slice adherence) so that findings are specialized and orthogonal.
15. As a developer reading review output, I want findings rendered as a single tabular report sorted CRITICAL → LOW so that I can triage at a glance.
16. As a developer with CRITICAL or HIGH findings, I want a numbered auto-fix prompt offering inline execution or follow-up beads tasks so that critical issues never wait.
17. As a developer using the slicer, I want one acceptance criterion per slice (or a tightly clustered set) so that each slice delivers user-visible value end-to-end.
18. As a developer using the slicer, I want a sizing check that halts and proposes sub-splits when a slice exceeds ~10 files or ~300 LOC so that PRs stay reviewable in under 30 minutes.
19. As a developer who has installed specwright in a JavaScript / Python / Rust / Go / Terraform project, I want the auto-verify loop to detect my project's commands automatically from manifests so that I don't configure anything for common ecosystems.
20. As a developer with non-standard verify commands, I want a `## Specwright — Verify Commands` section in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md as the override slot so that the project's preferred commands ship with the repo.
21. As a developer the first time verify fails to detect commands, I want the agent to ask once and propose persisting the answer into CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md so that I never re-answer the same question.
22. As a developer storing specs alongside code, I want PRDs in `.specs/<slug>/` (requirements.md + design.md + bugfix.md + TASKS.md) so that the PR introducing the spec is fully self-documenting.
23. As a developer reading a PRD, I want requirements.md in EARS notation so that acceptance criteria are unambiguous and machine-parseable.
24. As a developer reading a PRD, I want design.md to include mermaid diagrams (sequence + data flow) so that architecture is visual.
25. As a developer with multiple slices, I want a `TASKS.md` mirror auto-generated from beads so that the slice list is readable from the PR diff without leaving git.
26. As a user installing on Claude Code, I want a one-line `/plugin install specwright` so that setup is trivial.
27. As a user on Codex, I want to add the repo as a marketplace via `codex /plugins` so that I get the same skills with no manual file copying.
28. As a user on any other agent, I want to `git clone` the repo and copy `skills/` into my agent's skill directory so that the plugin remains portable.
29. As a team member working in the same repo, I want the spec PR to include the PRD changes so that I can review intent and implementation together.
30. As an agent reading the specwright project itself, I want a `CONTEXT.md` glossary defining slice / cohort / chain / mirror / etc. so that vocabulary stays consistent across sessions.
31. As a user encountering an ambiguous prompt in quick flow, I want the skill to bail to feature flow when major interpretations conflict so that I'm not committed to a one-shot misread.
32. As a developer who calls `/specwright` with no subcommand, I want the umbrella router to ask one or two sizing questions and dispatch to the right flow so that I don't memorize the four entries.
33. As a developer using the tiny flow, I want the entire spec — intent, AC, slice list — to live in a single beads issue body so that there's no on-disk overhead for trivial work.
34. As a developer reviewing a tiny-flow PR, I want a lightweight single-reviewer review instead of four-subagent fan-out so that token cost matches ticket size.
35. As a maintainer of specwright, I want fixture validators for each shared reference doc (spec-format, slice-schema, verify-discovery, review-format, stacking-rules) so that schema drift between skills and references is caught in CI.

## Implementation Decisions

### Skill graph

**Forked + adapted from the user's existing skills (5):** `/specwright:grill-me`, `/specwright:grill-with-docs`, `/specwright:tdd`, `/specwright:to-prd`, `/specwright:to-issues`. Each is adapted to Kiro style — `to-prd` produces requirements.md (EARS) + design.md (mermaid); `to-issues` produces beads slices with `depends_on` and `estimated_touched_paths` metadata; `tdd` is adapted to enforce intent-based tests; the grilling skills feed requirements.md and update `CONTEXT.md` inline. Explicitly **not forked:** `triage`, `handoff`.

**New orchestrator skills (10):**

- `/specwright` — umbrella router; 1–2 sizing questions → dispatch
- `/specwright:feature`, `:bugfix`, `:quick`, `:tiny` — entry-point flows
- `/specwright:slice` — AC-driven slicer; writes beads with `depends_on` and path metadata
- `/specwright:fanout` — gtr worktrees + native parallel subagent spawn (no shell fallback)
- `/specwright:execute` — per-slice six-step pipeline
- `/specwright:review` — four-subagent fan-out + tabular report + numbered auto-fix prompt
- `/specwright:resolve-conflict` — single auto-attempt on PR rebase failure

### Deep modules (shared references in `references/`)

These are the stable contracts skills consume. They are the tested surface of the plugin:

- `spec-format.md` — EARS requirements + mermaid design + bugfix three-section schema
- `slice-schema.md` — beads slice metadata contract: `{title, acceptance_criteria, depends_on, estimated_touched_paths, spec_path}`
- `verify-discovery.md` — `## Specwright — Verify Commands` section format + per-ecosystem fallback table
- `review-format.md` — finding schema `{severity, file:line, concern, why, recommended_fix}` + severity rules + tabular output spec
- `stacking-rules.md` — PR base-branch resolution rules + rebase / conflict-resolution semantics

### Storage hybrid

PRDs on disk in `.specs/<slug>/`; tasks in beads. `TASKS.md` mirror is auto-generated, never hand-edited. Tiny flow writes no `.specs/<slug>/` and stores the spec in a single beads issue body. See ADR 0001 for the trade-off rationale.

### Parallelism model

Slice = unit of parallelism = one beads issue. `depends_on` edges drive the dependency graph. `/specwright:fanout` groups the ready set into cohorts so no two slices in a cohort share an estimated touched path. Chains never fan out; they auto-stack as PRs via `gh pr create --base <parent-slice-branch>`. GitHub auto-retargets dependent PRs when their parent merges.

### Execute pipeline (six steps)

Load context (beads slice + PRD) → branch (base = parent's branch if stacked) → TDD via forked `/specwright:tdd` (RED-GREEN-REFACTOR, tests written against ACs as user-visible behavior) → auto-verify loop with N=3 retry cap → commit + push → open PR with body auto-generated from ACs.

### Verify command discovery (no config file)

(1) Read `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` for a `## Specwright — Verify Commands` section. (2) Fall back to per-ecosystem defaults (`package.json` scripts for JS/TS; `pytest` + `ruff` + `mypy`/`pyright` for Python; `cargo test`/`clippy`/`fmt`/`check` for Rust; `go test`/`vet`/`gofmt` for Go; `terraform fmt -check -recursive` + `tflint` for Terraform; `Makefile`/`justfile` targets override). (3) On miss, ask once and propose persistence as a `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` edit.

### Review

Four parallel subagents (spec-alignment, test-quality, code-quality + security, vertical-slice adherence) each emit findings as `{severity, file:line, concern, why, recommended_fix}`. Main skill merges into one tabular report sorted CRITICAL → LOW. After the table, a numbered prompt offers auto-fix scopes (`[1]` all CRITICAL, `[2]` CRITICAL+HIGH, `[3]` pick individually, `[4]` file as new beads tasks, `[5]` skip). Selected items run inline as `/specwright:execute` mini-runs or become follow-up beads slices.

### PR stacking + conflict resolution

Raw `git` + `gh`. Chained PRs created with `gh pr create --base <parent-slice-branch>`. On rebase failure after a sibling merges, `/specwright:resolve-conflict` makes a single auto-attempt: reads both diffs, semantically re-applies, runs tests, force-pushes on green; on red or unresolvable, comments on the PR with annotated diffs and hands back to the user.

### Bugfix flow specifics

Mandatory 2-slice split: `[1]` failing regression test (RED only, no fix) and `[2]` fix + Unchanged behavior still green. Slice 2 `depends_on` slice 1; they auto-stack as PRs. The review test-quality reviewer adds an extra check: did the regression test actually fail before the fix? Verified by running tests against slice-1's commit.

### Distribution

One git repo containing:

- `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — source of truth for all skills (markdown + YAML frontmatter)
- `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` — Codex manifest
- Claude Code plugin manifest
- `marketplace.json` — self-hosted Codex marketplace at repo root
- `references/` — shared reference docs
- `docs/adr/` — architecture decision records

## Testing Decisions

### What makes a good test

Tests verify **external contract**, not internal mechanics. For specwright, the external contract is the schema each shared-reference doc declares. A test passes if and only if a fixture conforming to the doc's stated schema parses correctly, and a counter-fixture violating the schema is rejected. Tests must never inspect skill internals (the markdown body of a SKILL.md), only inputs and outputs.

### Modules tested

All five shared-reference docs in `references/` get fixture validators:

1. **`spec-format.md`** — fixture set: sample `requirements.md` (EARS-valid), sample `design.md` (mermaid-parseable), sample `bugfix.md` (three sections present). Validator: EARS parser checks AC syntax; mermaid block check; bugfix section presence.
2. **`slice-schema.md`** — fixture set: sample beads slice JSON exports, both well-formed and counter-examples with missing required fields. Validator: JSON schema check.
3. **`verify-discovery.md`** — fixture set: sample `CLAUDE.md` files with and without the `## Specwright — Verify Commands` section; sample `package.json` / `pyproject.toml` / `Cargo.toml` / `Makefile` for ecosystem fallback. Validator: discovery function returns the expected command map.
4. **`review-format.md`** — fixture set: sample review-output JSON (well-formed); counter-examples missing required fields; counter-examples with invalid severities. Validator: JSON schema check + severity enum check.
5. **`stacking-rules.md`** — fixture set: sample beads dep graphs (linear chain, multiple chains, no deps) + expected base-branch resolution. Validator: pure function over the slice graph.

### Skills are not unit-tested

Skill prompts don't unit-test usefully — the LLM output is non-deterministic. Instead, a single integration smoke test runs `/specwright:slice` against a fixture PRD in a fixture repo and validates the produced beads slices against `slice-schema.md`'s validator. This is enough to catch the most common drift (slice metadata not matching the schema docs claim) without requiring an LLM in CI.

### Prior art

- EARS-validation libraries: `ears-checker` (Node) — for `spec-format.md` EARS rule
- JSON-schema validation: `ajv` (Node) / `jsonschema` (Python) — for slice-schema and review-format validators
- Kiro's spec validation patterns (referenced in `docs/how-kiro-does-it.md`)
- The user's existing `quality-gate` skill, which runs `code-quality-verifier` agent (analogous specialized-reviewer pattern; we extend to four subagents)

## Out of Scope

- **Alternative trackers (jira, linear, github-issues).** v1 is beads-only. Companion plugins later override `/specwright:slice` and `/specwright:fanout`.
- **Shell-script fan-out fallback.** Native subagent + worktree only; environments lacking the primitive get sequential execution.
- **Spec-drift continuous-validation.** Review is the only check that spec matches implementation; no background validator in v1.
- **Quick flow fully no-gate.** The single OK gate before fan-out is mandatory; no flag removes it.
- **Init skill / `.specwright/config.json`.** Strict convention-over-config.
- **CLI / daemon.** Pure skills bundle.
- **Forks of `triage` and `handoff` skills.** Explicitly excluded.
- **Stacking-tool integrations (Graphite, spr).** Raw git + gh only.
- **PRD localisation / non-English EARS variants.**
- **Plugin auto-update mechanism.** Users update via marketplace UI.

## Further Notes

- **Forked-skill licensing & attribution** (unresolved): the source skills live in the user's private `~/.claude/skills/`. Re-licensing for a public marketplace plugin (likely MIT) and attribution back to the user's collection both need a decision before first publish.
- **Codex Plugin Directory:** OpenAI's official directory publishing is "coming soon"; v1 ships self-hosted `marketplace.json` only.
- **Model selection** (unresolved): whether to hard-code Opus for review and Sonnet for execute, or detect from environment, is open.
- **Slice-size override prompt** (unresolved): whether the sizing-check halt interrupts a fully AFK flow or proceeds with a warning is open.
- **Quick-flow ambiguity-detection threshold** (unresolved): needs a concrete heuristic for "too ambiguous to one-shot."
- **Tiny-flow auto-routing trigger** (unresolved): how the umbrella `/specwright` decides an ask is tiny without asking — token count, keywords, or always ask explicitly — is open.
- **Schema-migration conflict resolution** (unresolved): whether `/specwright:resolve-conflict` handles schema-migration conflicts or always surfaces to the user is open.
- This PRD is the v1 epic. Slicing into beads child issues is a separate step (`/specwright:slice` self-hosted on this PRD once the project bootstraps).
- All decisions are sourced from the grilling session in this conversation, locked into `PLAN.md`, with terminology fixed in `CONTEXT.md` and the storage trade-off recorded in `docs/adr/0001-hybrid-spec-storage.md`.

title: specwright: /specwright umbrella router with sizing questions
description:
## Parent

specwright-bi2

## What to build

`/specwright` (no subcommand) — the umbrella router that asks 1–2 sizing questions and dispatches to `:feature`, `:bugfix`, `:quick`, or `:tiny`. The discoverable entry-point that a user can call when they're unsure which flow fits.

Behavior:

1. If invoked with an argument (e.g. `/specwright "fix the typo"`), the skill first checks for obvious signals — keywords like "typo", "rename", "label", short text length — and auto-routes to `:tiny`.
2. Otherwise asks question 1: "What's the shape of this work?" with options: (a) New feature / capability, (b) Bug fix, (c) I know exactly what to build — generate everything quickly, (d) Small ticket — skip the PRD.
3. Conditionally asks question 2 only if (a) was chosen: "Is the design well-understood? If yes I'll use quick flow; if no I'll do the full grill" — this lets users bypass `:feature` for clear work.
4. Dispatches to the matching flow skill with the user's original argument (if any) forwarded.

Auto-routing keywords for tiny (configurable, but defaults stated in skill body): "typo", "rename", "label", "comment", "docstring", "version bump", "dependency update" — all with the size check that the ask is < ~10 words.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `skills/specwright/SKILL.md` present with the routing logic
- [ ] No-arg invocation asks question 1
- [ ] With-arg invocation checks keywords + size, auto-routes to `:tiny` on match
- [ ] Question 2 only asked when question 1 = (a) New feature
- [ ] Dispatch correctly forwards the user's argument to the chosen flow skill
- [ ] Smoke test: each of the four flows reachable through the router
- [ ] Both manifests declare the bare `/specwright` skill name

## Blocked by

- Slice 13 (`:tiny`)
- Slice 14 (`:feature`)
- Slice 15 (`:bugfix`)
- Slice 16 (`:quick`)

title: specwright: /specwright:quick flow with assumptions + OK gate
description:
## Parent

specwright-bi2

## What to build

`/specwright:quick "<prompt>"` — Kiro-style quick flow. Single auto-generation pass through requirements.md + design.md + slices + TASKS.md, with every assumption surfaced and exactly one user OK gate before fan-out.

Pipeline:

1. **Single auto-gen pass** — invoke `/specwright:to-prd` and `/specwright:slice` back-to-back without approval gates between phases. Skill body explicitly disables the per-phase gates.
2. **Assumptions section** — agent writes a dated `## Assumptions` section at the top of `requirements.md`, each item phrased "Assumed X because Y." Every guess goes here.
3. **Ambiguity guard** — if the prompt is too ambiguous (the skill can't pick between plausible major interpretations), it bails to `/specwright:feature` with the reason. The "too ambiguous" threshold needs a concrete heuristic — see Further Notes in PRD; for v1, use: bail if two or more distinct primary user stories could be the intent and the prompt provides no disambiguator.
4. **One OK gate** — print a tight summary: "Here's what I generated. Here are the N assumptions. Want to proceed to fan-out? [Y/n]" — wait for explicit Y.
5. **Fan-out** — on Y, invoke `/specwright:fanout`. On n or anything else, halt and leave the artifacts on disk for the user to edit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `skills/specwright-quick/SKILL.md` present with the five-step pipeline
- [ ] Per-phase gates between to-prd and slice are explicitly disabled
- [ ] `## Assumptions` section is dated and lists every guess in "Assumed X because Y" format
- [ ] Ambiguity-guard heuristic stated explicitly in the skill body
- [ ] On ambiguity bail, the skill invokes `/specwright:feature` with the reason
- [ ] The OK gate accepts only an explicit Y to proceed; any other input halts
- [ ] Smoke test on a clear prompt: full flow runs to PRs. On an ambiguous prompt: bails to feature flow.
- [ ] Both manifests declare `:quick`

## Blocked by

- Slice 7 (forked `:to-prd`)
- Slice 9 (`:slice`)
- Slice 10 (`:review`)
- Slice 11 (`:fanout`)

title: specwright: /specwright:bugfix flow with mandatory 2-slice split
description:
## Parent

specwright-bi2

## What to build

`/specwright:bugfix "<bug description>"` — the diagnose-first bugfix flow with mandatory regression-test slice. Distinct from feature flow because the artifact shape (`bugfix.md`) and slicing rules (forced 2-slice split) differ.

Pipeline:

1. **Diagnose** — agent reads the bug report, attempts to reproduce locally (runs the failing case to confirm). If reproduction fails, bail to the user with the reproduction attempt details — do NOT proceed to write anything.
2. **Bugfix.md** — invoke `/specwright:to-prd` in bugfix mode to write `.specs/<slug>/bugfix.md` with the three sections from `spec-format.md`: Current Behavior (with code refs), Expected Behavior (in EARS), Unchanged Behavior (explicit non-regression list).
3. **Slice** — invoke `/specwright:slice` in bugfix mode, which emits exactly 2 slices: [1] failing regression test (RED only, no fix) and [2] fix + Unchanged behavior still green. Slice 2 `depends_on` slice 1 → auto-stacked PRs.
4. **Fan-out (sequential)** — `/specwright:fanout` will see only one ready slice at a time due to the dep chain; PRs stack.
5. **Review** — `/specwright:review` 4-subagent mode with the extra "did regression test fail before fix" check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `skills/specwright-bugfix/SKILL.md` present with diagnose-first behavior
- [ ] Diagnose step actually reproduces the bug; bails with explanation if it can't
- [ ] `bugfix.md` has all three sections per `spec-format.md`
- [ ] Slice exactly produces 2 beads issues with slice 2 `depends_on` slice 1
- [ ] PRs auto-stack via raw-git base resolution
- [ ] Review confirms regression test failed before the fix commit (runs tests on slice-1's commit)
- [ ] Smoke test end-to-end against a fixture bug repo
- [ ] Both manifests declare `:bugfix`

## Blocked by

- Slice 8 (`:execute`)
- Slice 9 (`:slice` — needed in bugfix mode)
- Slice 10 (`:review`)
- Slice 11 (`:fanout`)

title: specwright: /specwright:feature flow
description:
## Parent

specwright-bi2

## What to build

`/specwright:feature "<description>"` — the full three-phase Kiro flow. The most comprehensive entry-point: produces a PRD on disk, beads slices, parallel execution, and four-subagent review.

Pipeline:

1. **Grill** — invoke `/specwright:grill-with-docs` (uncapped). Resolves vocabulary, updates `CONTEXT.md`, offers ADRs sparingly.
2. **PRD** — invoke `/specwright:to-prd` to write `.specs/<slug>/requirements.md` (EARS) + `.specs/<slug>/design.md` (mermaid) to disk.
3. **Slice** — invoke `/specwright:slice` to write beads slices + `.specs/<slug>/TASKS.md` mirror.
4. **Fan-out** — invoke `/specwright:fanout` to launch parallel runners in worktrees.
5. **Review** — `/specwright:review` runs per PR (four-subagent mode) as each PR opens.

Each phase is gated by the user (per `/grill-with-docs` / Kiro approval-gate convention) except in `:quick` mode (which is slice 16). The feature skill body documents the gate prompts and what the user is shown at each.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `skills/specwright-feature/SKILL.md` present with the full five-step pipeline
- [ ] Each phase invokes the right delegate skill (grill-with-docs, to-prd, slice, fanout, review)
- [ ] Approval gates exist between phases with clear prompts
- [ ] CONTEXT.md updates happen inline during grilling
- [ ] PRD on disk passes `spec-format.md` validator
- [ ] Beads slices pass `slice-schema.md` validator
- [ ] Smoke test end-to-end: invoke `/specwright:feature "<small fixture feature>"`, observe PRD + slices + parallel PRs + 4-subagent reviews
- [ ] Both manifests declare `:feature`

## Blocked by

- Slice 7 (forked utilities — needs `:grill-with-docs`, `:to-prd`)
- Slice 9 (`:slice`)
- Slice 10 (`:review` 4-subagent mode)
- Slice 11 (`:fanout`)

title: specwright: /specwright:tiny flow
description:
## Parent

specwright-bi2

## What to build

`/specwright:tiny "<short ask>"` — the lightest entry-point flow. Skips PRDs entirely; stores the spec in a single beads issue body; uses lightweight review. The first user-visible flow specwright ships.

Pipeline:

1. **Brief grill** — invoke `/specwright:grill-me` in a capped variant (2–3 questions max) confirming intent + acceptance criteria. Skill body explicitly tells grill-me to stop after 3 questions.
2. **Write beads issue** — single beads slice with the intent, ACs, and a compact slice list in the body. No `.specs/<slug>/` directory created. Conforms to `slice-schema.md`'s tiny-variant (spec_path: null).
3. **Execute** — invoke `/specwright:execute` directly (no `:fanout` for tiny — only 1–2 slices, sequential is fine).
4. **Lightweight review** — invoke `/specwright:review` in single-subagent mode. CRITICAL/HIGH auto-fix prompt still applies.

Auto-routing: when the umbrella `/specwright` router (slice 17) detects an obviously-small ask, it dispatches here without explicit invocation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `skills/specwright-tiny/SKILL.md` present with the four-step pipeline
- [ ] Brief grill is capped at 2–3 questions (skill body enforces this verbatim)
- [ ] No `.specs/<slug>/` directory is created — spec body lives in the beads issue
- [ ] Beads issue conforms to `slice-schema.md`'s tiny-variant (spec_path: null)
- [ ] Review runs in lightweight (single-subagent) mode
- [ ] Smoke test end-to-end: invoke `/specwright:tiny "fix README typo"`, observe brief grill → beads issue → branch + PR + lightweight review report
- [ ] Both manifests declare `:tiny`

## Blocked by

- Slice 7 (forked `:grill-me`)
- Slice 8 (`:execute`)
- Slice 10 (`:review` lightweight mode)

title: specwright: /specwright:resolve-conflict single-attempt rebase resolver
description:
## Parent

specwright-bi2

## What to build

`/specwright:resolve-conflict` — single-auto-attempt PR rebase + conflict resolver. Triggers automatically when a sibling PR merges and the next PR in a chain fails to rebase onto the new main. Falls back to surfacing the conflict to the user on failure.

Algorithm (per `references/stacking-rules.md`):

1. Detect rebase failure on a stacked PR.
2. Read both diffs: the merged sibling's diff + this PR's diff.
3. Apply this PR's changes semantically on top of the merged base (the agent reads both, understands the intent, re-implements where necessary).
4. Run the project's test suite (discovered per `verify-discovery.md`).
5. On green: commit the resolution, force-push the PR branch, comment on the PR noting the auto-resolution.
6. On red OR unresolvable: open a PR comment with both diffs annotated, mark the slice `blocked` in beads, notify the user. Single auto-attempt cap — do NOT retry.

Triggers:

- Called automatically from `/specwright:execute` when its branch step detects the parent has merged and rebase fails.
- Called manually as `/specwright:resolve-conflict <pr#>` for user-initiated cleanups.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `skills/specwright-resolve-conflict/SKILL.md` present with the full algorithm
- [ ] Single-attempt cap is enforced and stated explicitly
- [ ] On green resolution: force-push + PR comment + beads slice stays in current status
- [ ] On red/unresolvable: PR comment with annotated diffs + beads slice marked `blocked`
- [ ] Manual invocation `/specwright:resolve-conflict <pr#>` works against any open PR
- [ ] Test suite discovery uses `references/verify-discovery.md`
- [ ] Smoke test: simulate sibling-merge + rebase failure on a fixture repo; verify auto-resolution end-to-end on a trivial conflict, verify user-handback on a non-trivial one
- [ ] Both manifests declare `:resolve-conflict`

- Slice 6 (stacking-rules.md)
- Slice 8 (`:execute`)

title: specwright: /specwright:fanout parallel runner with cohort grouping
description:
## Parent

specwright-bi2

## What to build

`/specwright:fanout` — parallel runner that converts the beads ready set into concurrent worktree-isolated subagent executions. Reads beads, computes cohorts that share no `estimated_touched_paths`, creates one worktree per cohort member via `gtr`, spawns sub-agents in each via the host's native parallel primitive (Claude Code `Agent` tool with `isolation: worktree`; Codex equivalent). No shell-script fallback.

Behavior:

1. Query beads for ready set (slices with all `depends_on` parents `done`).
2. Compute cohorts via path-overlap detection per `references/slice-schema.md` — two slices share a cohort only if their `estimated_touched_paths` glob sets do not intersect.
3. For each cohort member: create a worktree via `gtr` (trust the user's `.gtrconfig` for copy rules; do not manage gtr config), spawn a sub-agent that invokes `/specwright:execute <slice-id>`.
4. Report progress as sub-agents complete; on a sub-agent return, mark the slice `done` in beads (if execute already did so, this is a no-op).
5. On cohort completion, re-query beads (newly unblocked slices may now be ready), compute the next cohort, repeat until ready set is empty.

The skill explicitly does NOT fall back to a shell script when the host lacks native parallel subagents — that environment gets sequential execution by invoking `:execute` directly. The skill detects this and emits a clear message.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `skills/specwright-fanout/SKILL.md` present with cohort algorithm and worktree spawn logic
- [ ] Cohort grouping uses pure path-overlap detection from `estimated_touched_paths`
- [ ] Worktrees are created via `gtr` only — no direct `git worktree add` calls
- [ ] Sub-agents are spawned via the host's native primitive; no shell-script fallback
- [ ] On hosts without native parallel subagents, the skill explicitly falls back to sequential `:execute` invocations and reports this
- [ ] Smoke test: 3 ready slices with non-overlapping paths execute in parallel; 3 with overlapping paths serialize into cohorts
- [ ] Re-query after each cohort picks up newly-unblocked dependents
- [ ] Both manifests declare `:fanout`

`/specwright:review` — the four-subagent code-review fan-out plus a lightweight single-subagent mode for tiny flow. Both emit findings per `references/review-format.md` and the main skill merges them into the tabular report + numbered auto-fix prompt.

Four subagents (each isolated context, run in parallel):

- **Spec alignment** — PR diff vs `.specs/<slug>/requirements.md` + `design.md`; flags drift, missing ACs, scope creep.
- **Test quality** — do tests verify user-visible behavior or implementation details? Vertical-slice coverage? Mocks-at-boundaries-only? Extra check in bugfix flow: did the regression test actually fail before the fix? (Verified by running tests against slice-1's commit.)
- **Code quality + security** — codebase patterns, complexity, OWASP top-10, secret leaks.
- **Vertical-slice adherence** — did the PR stay inside the slice's `estimated_touched_paths`? Reviewable in <30 min?

Lightweight mode: a single subagent that combines spec + test + code concerns into one pass for tiny flow.

After merging findings into the sorted tabular report (CRITICAL → LOW), emit the numbered auto-fix prompt with the five choices from `review-format.md`. Selected fixes either run inline as `/specwright:execute` mini-runs or get created as follow-up beads slices linked back to the original.

title: specwright: /specwright:slice AC-driven cutter + TASKS.md mirror
description:
## Parent

## What to build

`/specwright:slice` — the AC-driven vertical-slice cutter. Reads a PRD from `.specs/<slug>/requirements.md` + `design.md` (or `bugfix.md`) and writes beads slices conforming to `references/slice-schema.md`. Also generates the `.specs/<slug>/TASKS.md` mirror.

Behavior:

- **Cut rule:** one user-visible acceptance criterion per slice (or a tight cluster of co-dependent ACs that can't be delivered separately). Slice metadata (touched paths, depends_on) is derived from `design.md`'s component map + a repo grep.
- **Sizing check:** estimate each slice's size from design.md components × rough complexity. If a slice exceeds ~10 files touched OR ~300 LOC estimated, the skill halts and asks the user: "AC X looks too big. Split into [proposed sub-slices A, B] or proceed anyway?" — user can always override.
- **TASKS.md mirror:** auto-generated snapshot of beads slices with their `depends_on` graph. Regenerated on every invocation. Header warns "auto-generated; do not hand-edit."
- **Bugfix mode:** when invoked on a `bugfix.md`, emit exactly 2 slices: [1] failing regression test (RED only), [2] fix + Unchanged behavior still green. Slice 2 `depends_on` slice 1.

Delegates writing to the forked `/specwright:to-issues` skill so beads creation stays consistent.

title: specwright: /specwright:execute six-step per-slice pipeline
description:
## Parent

specwright-bi2

## What to build

`/specwright:execute` — the six-step per-slice pipeline that runs inside a worktree from "slice is ready in beads" to "PR open." This is the workhorse of every flow.

Steps (skill body documents and orchestrates each):

1. **Load context** — read the beads slice (acceptance criteria, `depends_on`, `estimated_touched_paths`, `spec_path`); if `spec_path` is set, load `requirements.md` + `design.md`.
2. **Branch** — `slice/<beads-id>-<kebab-slug>` per `stacking-rules.md`; base = parent slice's branch if `depends_on` and parent PR open, else `main`.
3. **TDD** — delegate to `/specwright:tdd`. RED tests written against the slice's ACs (verbatim from beads), framed as user-visible behavior. GREEN minimum implementation. REFACTOR.
4. **Auto-verify loop** — run all commands discovered per `references/verify-discovery.md`. On failure, the agent reads the output and fixes. Capped at **N=3 retries**. On cap, mark the slice `blocked` in beads with the failure output attached and surface to the user.
5. **Commit + push** — semantic commit message, co-author trailer (read from `git config user.name` + `user.email`).
6. **Open PR** — `gh pr create --base <resolved-base-branch>`, body auto-generated from the slice's ACs + a link to `spec_path`. Mark the beads slice `done`.

The skill preamble carries the vertical-slice reminder: if the agent finds itself making changes outside the slice's `estimated_touched_paths`, it pauses and reports rather than proceeding.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `skills/specwright-execute/SKILL.md` present with frontmatter and full pipeline body
- [ ] Pipeline references `references/verify-discovery.md` for command discovery
- [ ] Pipeline references `references/slice-schema.md` for beads metadata reading
- [ ] Pipeline references `references/stacking-rules.md` for base-branch resolution
- [ ] Retry cap is exactly N=3 and is stated explicitly in the skill body
- [ ] On retry-cap exhaustion, the skill marks the beads slice `blocked` with `bd update --status blocked` and appends the failure output as a note
- [ ] Smoke test: hand-create a beads slice in a fixture repo, invoke the skill, observe branch + PR + beads status update

title: specwright: stacking-rules.md reference contract + validator
description:

## What to build

`references/stacking-rules.md` — the canonical contract for how chained slices become stacked PRs and how `/specwright:resolve-conflict` handles rebase failures.

Document:

- PR base-branch resolution: if a slice has `depends_on: [parent-slice-id]` and that parent slice's PR is open, the new PR's base is the parent's branch (`gh pr create --base <parent-slice-branch>`); else base is the repo default (`main`). For multi-parent slices, fall back to the first parent's branch and document why (most chains are linear in practice).
- Branch naming convention: `slice/<beads-id>-<kebab-slug>` so branches are identifiable from beads ID alone.
- Rebase semantics on parent merge: GitHub auto-retargets; specwright does not interfere.
- Conflict resolution algorithm: when `git rebase` fails, `/specwright:resolve-conflict` reads both diffs, applies the new diff semantically on top of the merged base, runs tests; on green force-pushes; on red opens a PR comment with annotated diffs and stops. Single auto-attempt cap.

Fixture validator: pure function taking a slice graph (beads dep edges) + the current state of open/merged PRs, and returns the expected base branch for each slice's PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `references/stacking-rules.md` documents PR base-branch resolution with examples (linear chain, multi-chain, no deps)
- [ ] Document specifies branch naming convention exactly
- [ ] Conflict-resolution algorithm documented with the single-attempt cap explicit

title: specwright: review-format.md reference contract + validator
description:
## Parent

## What to build

`references/review-format.md` — the canonical contract for review subagent findings, severity rules, and the merged tabular output. Both the lightweight (tiny-flow) review path and the four-subagent (feature/bugfix/quick) review path emit findings in this schema; `/specwright:review` merges them.

Schema (per finding):

- `severity` — one of CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW
- `file` — repo-relative path
- `line` — integer line number (or range)
- `concern` — short tag (e.g. "spec drift", "test couples to internals")
- `why` — free-text explanation
- `recommended_fix` — actionable fix proposal

Severity rules:

- CRITICAL: security vulnerability, data loss, scope drift large enough that PRD acceptance fails
- HIGH: missing acceptance criterion, test that fails to verify intent, OWASP top-10 issue
- MEDIUM: code-quality concerns, pattern divergence, complexity over threshold
- LOW: nits, naming, optional improvements

Tabular output: markdown table `| Severity | Concern | Location | Why | Fix |`, sorted CRITICAL → LOW. After the table, the numbered auto-fix prompt with five fixed choices.

Fixture validator: load sample review-output JSON exports from `tests/fixtures/review-format/`, check each finding conforms to schema and severity enum, check tabular renderer produces deterministic output sorted correctly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `references/review-format.md` documents the finding schema, severity rules, and tabular output spec
- [ ] At least 5 positive and 5 negative finding fixtures (mixed severities, malformed)
- [ ] Validator runs in CI and rejects findings with invalid severity, missing required fields, malformed line refs
- [ ] Tabular renderer fixture produces byte-identical output for the same input

## What to build

`references/verify-discovery.md` — the canonical contract for how `/specwright:execute`'s auto-verify loop finds the test/lint/format/typecheck/build commands at runtime, given that specwright ships no init skill and no config file.

Document the three-stage discovery algorithm:

1. Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` (whichever or both the project has) for a `## Specwright — Verify Commands` section. Specify the exact heading and the fenced block format the section uses.
2. Fall back to per-ecosystem defaults. Provide the canonical table: JS/TS `package.json` scripts; Python `pytest` + `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy`/`pyright`; Rust `cargo test` + `clippy` + `fmt --check` + `check`; Go `go test ./...` + `vet` + `gofmt`; Terraform `terraform fmt -check -recursive` + `tflint`. `Makefile`/`justfile` targets named the same override.
3. On unresolved miss, ask the user once and **propose** a CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md edit to persist the answer.

Fixture validator: a function that takes a fixture project tree (some with the override section, some bare, some with Makefile overrides) and asserts it returns the expected command map per the algorithm. Counter-fixtures with malformed override sections should be ignored (algorithm falls through to defaults).
